newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures erode further late, end lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures erode further late, end lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures fell more in the last hour, with the long end sagging to moderate losses.

Traders said the final leg down in March Treasury bond futures appeared unrelated to any single event, but it caught napping those who had expected the contract to stick to a tight range before the week's first bit of important U.S. economic data on Tuesday.
"It looked like there was no trigger that we can find," said a Treasury bond futures floor analyst. "There were no comments, no large hedgers...but no one expected it (price drop) in front of ECI."
Tuesday's U.S. fourth quarter 1996 employment cost index is forecast on average gaining 0.9 percent versus a 0.6-percent increase in the previous report.
"It was very quiet," said another broker of the initial downtick. "I think it was a function of a thin market."
The pullback increased in power, however, as dealers and banks began selling when nearby T-bonds neared and then sliced below support at 109-26/32, a three-month low set January 10.
Large sell-stops were triggered at that level, and selling briefly snowballed before bidders started emerging at about 109-22/32 and stemmed the decline, they added.
December durable goods Wednesday are expected to rise 1.2 percent and gain 2.2 percent excluding defense.
Friday's real advance fourth-quarter GDP is seen showing 3.9-percent growth with a 2.2-percent rise in the price index.

At settlement, March T-bonds fell 15/32 to 109-25/32, 10-year notes lost 8/32 to 107-23/32, muni-bonds dropped 11/32 to 113-22/32, March T-bills easd one bp to 94.90, and June Eurodollars declined three bps to 94.15. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
